The existing lab has four routers, 20 PCs and static IPv4 routing. A DNS server on **pc1 (10.14.1.11)** could serve all six LANs without changing their connections. The proposed configuration would use the existing `kathara/base` image, BIND9, and configure each PC to use pc1 as its resolver.

The DNS records would be:

| Name | Device | Address |
|---|---|---|
| `ai.research.lab.net` | pc12 | 10.14.4.12 |
| `data.research.lab.net` | pc13 | 10.14.4.13 |
| `shop.example.com` | pc8 | 10.14.3.11 |
| `ci.tools.net` | pc11 | 10.14.4.11 |
| `api.service.com` | pc9 | 10.14.3.12 |
| `mail.example.com` | pc4 | 10.14.1.14 |
| `mail.service.com` | pc5 | 10.14.2.11 |
| `mail.lab.net` | pc6 | 10.14.2.12 |
| `mail.tools.net` | pc7 | 10.14.2.13 |

Each of the four domains would have an MX record pointing to its corresponding `mail` name, with priority 10. These records identify mail destinations; they do not themselves provide an email service.

Implementation would add BIND configuration and zone files under pc1, start the service in `pc1.startup`, and configure DNS resolution in all PC startup files. Validation would check A and MX queries from PCs on different LANs, along with reachability of the returned addresses.

No files have been changed.
